quotes.text: The question is not whether artificial intelligence will shape our world, but whether we will harness it to strengthen the nation, improve daily life, and win the global AI race against adversaries like China. But as AI advances, so too do the threats we face. From China, Russia and Iran to sophisticated cybercriminal networks, adversaries are leveraging AI to increase the scale and complexity of attacks against the U.S., our infrastructure and our communities.

From AI to robotics, these systems aren’t just tools—they shape information, influence narratives, and, if compromised, can pose real physical threats to critical infrastructure.

Our national security, our economy, and our values depend on America leading in the AI race.

Every day, Chinese companies like DeepSeek and Unitree Robotics are exploiting American innovation and supporting China’s military activities. We cannot allow the CCP to further integrate its technology into American business operations, critical infrastructure, and autonomous platforms.

Proud to work with my colleagues on @HomelandGOP to prevent these supply chain security vulnerabilities.

The People’s Republic of China is moving aggressively to dominate the technologies that are reshaping the global economy and security, including artificial intelligence, robotics, and autonomous systems. This competition is already present on American campuses, in American police departments, on American smartphones, and increasingly within systems connected to our critical infrastructure.
Let me be clear about what that means. DeepSeek did not simply outcompete American companies. According to these disclosures, it stole from them.

American companies are innovating and competing seriously in robotics and artificial intelligence, and this Subcommittee strongly supports their work. The answer is not to retreat from these technologies. It is to invest in trusted American alternatives, strengthen cybersecurity practices, and prevent federal funds from supporting platforms that put American data and infrastructure at risk and give China an economic and military advantage.

Since the beginning of the Iran conflict, cyberattacks increased 245%. Additionally, last year marked an 89% increase in AI-enabled cyberattacks. The reality is clear — AI is fundamentally reshaping the cyber battlefield.

AI can identify weaknesses, analyze systems and accelerate cyber operations at a speed that was unimaginable just a few years ago. As adversaries gain access to these capabilities, we must ensure America’s defenders have the most advanced tools available to protect our critical infrastructure.

Today, I joined my colleagues on @HomelandGOP for a demo highlighting how innovation and technology are helping keep Americans safe 25 years after 9/11.

From K9 operations and drones to virtual reality and AI, these tools are giving our law enforcement new capabilities to detect threats, respond faster, and protect our communities.

The threats we face continue to evolve. Our technology must evolve with them.
